target.title: fix(browser): check existing-session wait navigation [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser `wait` predicates could continue in a replacement document before Browser navigation policy had approved that document. On managed Playwright, `waitForFunction` is recreated after an execution-context replacement. On existing-session Chrome MCP, the polling loop could evaluate again after navigation. A model-controlled predicate could therefore run on a policy-denied destination before the existing post-action check rejected the response.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep Playwright's native in-document scheduler and async-predicate semantics, but bind each guarded wait to one document handle. Only Playwright 1.61.1's exact cross-document JSHandle error causes a retry; policy is checked before capture and again before predicate execution in the replacement document. Infrastructure and user-predicate errors are never reclassified as navigation.
- Run existing-session waits as one exact Chrome MCP session transaction. A loader-bound root UID binds the predicate to one document; session replacement fails closed before another target can be touched, and only typed tool-level stale-document errors can rebind.
- Use one aggregate timeout/abort lifecycle, dispose handles unconditionally, avoid overlapping async predicate calls, and disconnect only truly wedged guarded evaluations.
- Pin the default launcher and document-bound compatibility gate to reviewed `chrome-devtools-mcp@1.5.0`. URL-only and time-only waits remain available to custom MCP servers; document-bound waits fail with an actionable version error rather than assuming an undocumented UID contract.
- Correct the custom launcher documentation: `mcpCommand` replaces the executable/default package prefix, while `mcpArgs` append after OpenClaw-managed arguments.

## User Impact

Allowed waits retain Playwright's native polling behavior and continue across approved navigation. A wait can no longer execute its predicate in a denied replacement document or silently move to a replacement Chrome MCP session. Existing-session users get a deterministic compatibility error for unreviewed MCP versions without losing URL-only or time-only waits.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `769990d8d4694360a25f70c79a71594ad0b6905a`
- Exact GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29044649180 - passed.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox `cbx_c8fcb69ca49d`, public networking, no Tailscale, no instance profile, IMDSv2 IAM endpoint 404, exact PR head verified, Node 24.15 / pnpm 11.2.2:
  - `run_185055c0c89d`: 5 focused files, 135/135 tests passed.
  - `run_34c095a5db0e`: `pnpm check:changed` passed, including extension production/test types, changed-file lint, dependency pins, import cycles, docs lane, and boundary guards.
  - Lease released after proof.
- Exact dependency audit:
  - Playwright Core 1.61.1: generic cross-document JSHandles throw the exact non-retriable context error used by the guard; its wait scheduler remains page-owned.
  - Chrome DevTools MCP 1.5.0: snapshot UIDs combine loader and backend-node identity; `evaluate_script` resolves UID arguments in their owning frame; server identity is `chrome_devtools 1.5.0`.
- Final whole-branch autoreview is being rerun after the lint-only follow-up; no clean result is claimed here until it completes.

Live Dev Gateway + OpenAI agent + real Browser navigation proof will be added before merge; it is intentionally not claimed by the current evidence.
